text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000133 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity band, including healthy patients, yet every documented 99215 in the small records sample was supported, so the evidence points both ways.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share appears in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions billed for routine-looking diagnoses such as abdominal pain, UTI or back pain (e.g., C0081763, C0082044, C0082449). That spread is the pattern of concern, since case mix alone does not explain it. Against this, all 20 documented 99215 claims were supported, including low-complexity claim C0082079 documented at high MDM. Taken at face value, that is consistent with legitimately complex visits. The records sample is thin, though (about 6% of claims), and the 27% 'problems' note-signal rate plus the absence of an audit trail mean the documentation could be inflated or templated to match billing; the 3 notes claiming moderate-plus data with no lab or test line are weak support for that. A reviewer should first pull charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed and request the EHR audit trail. The goal is to test whether high-MDM notes on zero- or one-condition patients reflect actual work or cloned content, and to check whether the two unsupported 99214s (C0082092, C0082164) hint at a broader leveling issue."}
